stemMd: Suppose Raman finds a boulder whose widest lichen is very nearly the same size as the widest lichens on boulders from a fall recorded 600 years ago. Based on the text, which choice is the most logical conclusion she can draw about this boulder?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The boulder was exposed several centuries ago, but the lichen cannot date its exposure to a particular century.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The boulder was exposed within the last 300 years, the range in which lichen size tracks recorded dates closely.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The lichen on the boulder began growing before the boulder's face was exposed, so the lichen is older than the fall.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The boulder was exposed about 600 years ago, within a few years of the recorded fall whose lichens it matches.

explanationMd:
An inference question asks for the strongest claim the text will actually carry — no stronger.

The text gives two facts that bear on this boulder. First, lichen size is a minimum age, and a lichen as wide as those on a 600-year-old fall is a large lichen, so the boulder is old. Second, beyond about 300 years the lichens' growth has slowed so much that Raman's estimates "bunched together, blurring events a century or more apart". Both facts together give exactly this: the boulder was exposed several centuries ago, but the lichen cannot date its exposure to a particular century.

To check an inference, look for a sentence in the passage that would contradict your choice or that your choice has to ignore. For that choice there is none. The choice claiming the boulder was exposed about 600 years ago, within a few years of the matching fall, has to ignore the blurring sentence, and that sentence is the text's whole point about old falls.

distractorRationale.d: This treats a blurred estimate as a precise one. The text says explicitly that past about 300 years the method cannot separate events a century or more apart, so matching the lichens of a 600-year-old fall does not pin this boulder to within a few years of 600.
distractorRationale.c: This contradicts the premise of the method. The passage describes lichens as colonising a face that begins as bare stone, so growth starts after exposure, not before it, and the lichen cannot be older than the fall.
distractorRationale.b: This reverses the reasoning. A very wide lichen indicates a long exposure; it is the small lichens that would indicate a recent fall. The under-300-year range is where dating is precise, but a lichen as wide as those on a 600-year-old fall lies beyond that range, not inside it.

accessibilityText: Using the lichen-dating passage, choose the most logical conclusion about a boulder whose widest lichen nearly matches the widest lichens on boulders from a rockfall recorded 600 years ago. The four choices say: that the boulder was exposed several centuries ago, but the lichen cannot date its exposure to a particular century; that the boulder was exposed within the last 300 years, the range in which lichen size tracks recorded dates closely; that the lichen began growing before the boulder's face was exposed, so the lichen is older than the fall; and that the boulder was exposed about 600 years ago, within a few years of the recorded fall whose lichens it matches.

provenance.notes: Original item. The scenario in the stem is new and is not stated in the passage, so the item tests inference rather than retrieval.

review.author: digital-sat-wave3-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Beyond about 300 years, lichen estimates bunch together and blur events a century or more apart. A match with a 600-year-old fall therefore shows only an old exposure, not one that can be dated to a particular century. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-sat-rw-run1) reached the same answer: Beyond about 300 years, the estimates bunch together, 'blurring events a century or more apart'. A boulder matching the 600-year fall is therefore old, several centuries, but cannot be pinned to a century. D claims precision the method lacks at that age. B contradicts the match. C has no support.]
